title: Choose the main menu's structure
question: Same world for all three: fog, grain, bone-white type, rust red, lantern amber. What changes is how the menu is built. Pick one; steer or re-roll if none fits.

options.label: Room 6 Key Rack
options.lineage: the Hollowmere motel's reception key board
options.thesis: The menu is the motel's key rack: every option is a rounded key fob with an icon, and the one you pick swings forward and tells you where it leads.
options.viewport: The live fog scene fills the screen. The logo is top-left. A horizontal row of six fobs hangs from a brass rail at the lower third. The selected fob drops forward under an amber light, and a save-preview card sits above it: chapter, place, play time, Mark %.
options.risk: The fobs could read as a novelty if the motion is cute rather than heavy; they have to swing like real metal.

options.label: Channel 7 Dial
options.lineage: Moth's pocket radio, Silent Hill's static
options.thesis: The menu is a radio band: options are stations along a dial at the bottom, a needle glides between them, and static fills the gaps.
options.viewport: The fog scene is full-bleed with the logo large and centred high. Along the bottom, a rounded glass dial carries six station marks, each with an icon and a frequency number. The amber needle sits on the selection, and its description reads above the dial like a broadcast.
options.risk: A horizontal dial is slower to scan than a column; deep pages (Load, Dev) need their own vertical layout.

options.label: Case Dossier
options.lineage: the missing-person file on Alex's sister
options.thesis: The menu is a case folder lying in the fog: rounded index tabs are the pages, and inside are a postcard, save slots as evidence cards, and the next step.
options.viewport: The fog scene is on the left 60%, with the logo over it. On the right, a dark folder with rounded tabs (Continue, New, Load, Extra) runs down its edge. The open tab shows the Continue card large: a polaroid of where you saved, the chapter and the objective.
options.risk: It's the most 'UI panel' of the three; without heavy material it slides toward a generic settings sheet.
